core_job: A family's on-device immigration case file. Each receipt carries its form type, the person it belongs to and its receipt date. Statuses are recorded by the user from the official USCIS site; the existing status log is kept, and the app adds days spent in each stage. The user can also record the processing time USCIS posts for their form and the Visa Bulletin cutoffs for their priority date. All of it rolls up into one offline "Docket" of upcoming windows, expiries and notice deadlines for every person. The app cannot fetch statuses: USCIS case-status and processing-times endpoints and travel.state.gov returned Cloudflare 403 to curl, and the official USCIS API needs credentials we do not have.
signature:
"Windows" plus the Citizenship clock.

Windows: filing windows are computed on the device from the user's own card expiry dates, with the rule quoted word for word from uscis.gov under each date (all pages fetched 2026-10-12):
- I-751: "90-day period immediately before your conditional residence expires".
- I-765 EAD renewal: "up to 180 days before", plus USCIS's "at least 90 days".
- I-90: "will expire within the next six months".
- N-400: "90 calendar days before" the 5-year anniversary, or the 3-year anniversary if married to a US citizen.

Citizenship clock: a trip log adjusts the N-400 picture. It gives the earliest filing date and counts physical-presence days against 913, counting departure and return days as days present (USCIS Policy Manual vol 12 D ch 4). It flags trips over 6 months and trips of 1 year or more (ch 3), and a "Plan a trip" what-if shows the effect of a trip before it is booked.

Competitors, checked through the iTunes API (descriptions only): Immivision (318k ratings) and Lawfully (173k) do live status but do not mention filing windows or trip counting. Green Card Trips (9 ratings) already does trip counting, and the spec says so. The claimed gap is narrow: one family file with rule-quoted windows for every card, plus the clock.
